findings.claim: unsubscribe returns a 500 when the logged-in user has no TopicUser row for the topic. TopicUser.find_by returns nil and the next line calls tu.notification_level on it.
findings.evidence: find_by(user_id:, topic_id:) is followed by tu.notification_level with no nil check, and ensure_logged_in is the only guard. open-code-review: mention, link and PM-invite emails are sent via PostAlerter without creating a row, and post_alerter.rb:22,105 already uses .try(:notification_level). The seats disagree on how often this happens: superpowers says the emailed recipient always has a row (user_notifications calls TopicUser.change with last_emailed_post_number), but all three agree on forwarded, shared or hand-typed links. All three propose the same controller spec, which expects NoMethodError on nil. Reasoned; not executed.
findings.reason: Accepted. Red test first: a controller spec with log_in, a fresh Fabricate(:topic), then get :unsubscribe, expecting success. Smallest fix: use TopicUser.change, which creates the missing row. The disagreement over how common the case is does not affect the crash path.

verifier.reason: At app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:105-107, unsubscribe calls TopicUser.find_by(user_id:, topic_id:) and then tu.notification_level with no nil check. Nothing earlier creates the row: ensure_logged_in only checks for a user, and TopicView.new (lib/topic_view.rb) never calls TopicUser.change, create or track_visit. A logged-in user with no TopicUser row for the topic therefore gets a NoMethodError, which surfaces as a 500.

findings.claim: A plain GET with no CSRF protection and no per-user token changes notification state. Any third-party page can change a logged-in visitor's level for any topic they can see, including PMs, for example with .
findings.evidence: Routes at config/routes.rb:440-441 are plain get. The action (topics_controller.rb:98-115) calls tu.save!. Rails CSRF protection skips GET, and skip_before_filter :check_xhr (line 32) lets plain navigations through. Unlike the digest route email/unsubscribe/:key (routes.rb:202), the link carries no signed key. Reasoned.
findings.reason: Accepted. Red test: a request spec showing that a cross-origin-style GET with no token changes notification_level. Smallest fix: mutate only on POST or with a signed per-user token, and keep the GET as a confirmation page. Severity stays Important even though superpowers notes the impact per hit is low.

verifier.reason: The patch adds plain GET routes for unsubscribe (config/routes.rb:444-445). They go to TopicsController#unsubscribe (app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:98-116), which needs only a session cookie (ensure_logged_in, line 28; check_xhr skipped, line 32), has no signed key or token, and calls tu.save! to set the level to regular or muted. Rails does not check CSRF tokens on GET, and the slug redirect at line 102 still reaches the action, so an on a third-party page can trigger it.

findings.claim: The action steps the level down instead of setting a target level, so it is not idempotent. Watching/tracking goes to regular on the first visit and regular goes to muted on a reload, second click or history replay, muting a topic the user never chose to mute.
findings.evidence: At topics_controller.rb:107-111, a level above regular is set to regular and any other level is set to muted. Two visits to a watching-topic email therefore produce muted. Reasoned.
findings.reason: Accepted. Red test: from watching, two GETs to unsubscribe should leave the same level as one GET; this fails on the pinned code. Smallest fix: set one fixed target level.

verifier.reason: In app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:107-111, unsubscribe lowers the level by one step: a level above regular becomes regular, and anything else becomes muted. Because this runs on every GET (routes.rb adds `get t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe`), a second visit, such as a reload, takes a watching or tracking topic from regular to muted.

findings.claim: After a watching/tracking user's first click the confirmation says 'You will stop receiving notifications for {{title}}', but the server only lowered the level to regular, which still notifies (and emails) on replies, mentions and quotes. The copy promises a state that was not set.
findings.evidence: Text at client.en.yml:985, rendered via controllers/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6:5-7 and templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs:3, compared with the level logic at topics_controller.rb:107-111. Severity varies by seat: Important as part of a larger finding in mattpocock and superpowers, Minor as a standalone finding in open-code-review. Normalised to Important. Reasoned.
findings.reason: Accepted. Red test: after one unsubscribe visit from watching, assert the user gets no reply notifications for the topic (level muted). This fails on the pinned code. Probably settled by the same fixed-target-level change as the idempotency finding; otherwise reword the copy.

verifier.reason: When the level is above regular, topics_controller.rb:206-207 only lowers it to regular, yet client.en.yml:984 (from the patch) always shows 'You will stop receiving notifications for {{title}}'. The app's own text for regular at client.en.yml:1101 says the user is still notified when someone mentions their @name or replies to them.

findings.claim: The new state-changing behaviour has no tests: TopicsController#unsubscribe, Topic#unsubscribe_url, the new email footer, the login requirement, the slug redirect, the missing-TopicUser path and the Ember route. This breaches CONTRIBUTING.md §3, 'Include tests, and ensure they pass'.
findings.evidence: The only spec change is spec/components/email/message_builder_spec.rb:171-172, which adds unsubscribe_url: so the existing spec keeps passing and asserts nothing about it. Nothing is added under spec/controllers. open-code-review rated this Minor; mattpocock and superpowers rated it Important.
findings.reason: Accepted. Settled by keeping the red-to-green controller specs written for the main-list fixes (nil TopicUser, CSRF GET, idempotency, copy) in the suite. No separate abstraction is needed.

verifier.reason: The patch changes only one spec file: spec/components/email/message_builder_spec.rb:511-513, where it passes unsubscribe_url to an existing fixture. spec/controllers/topics_controller_spec.rb has no unsubscribe test, and nothing tests TopicsController#unsubscribe (app/controllers/topics_controller.rb), Topic#unsubscribe_url or the new routes, which goes against CONTRIBUTING.md:42-44 ('Include tests, and ensure they pass').

findings.claim: A logged-out recipient who clicks the email link is redirected to '/' with no message and no return to the unsubscribe page, so nothing is unsubscribed.
findings.evidence: unsubscribe was added to ensure_logged_in; mattpocock cites line 27 and open-code-review line 28. rescue_from Discourse::NotLoggedIn (application_controller.rb:97-104) runs redirect_to path('/') for HTML GETs without storing a destination. Rated Minor by mattpocock and Important by open-code-review. Reasoned.
findings.reason: Appendix: two seats. Not reported as a review comment and not fixed this loop. ponytail named the same issue under 'outside my lane, not assessed', so it is not counted as a raising seat.

findings.claim: tu.save! bypasses TopicUser.change. As a result there is no MessageBus notification_level_change publish (other open tabs go stale), notifications_reason_id is not set to user_changed (the old reason text stays), and notifications_changed_at is not stamped.
findings.evidence: TopicUser.change (topic_user.rb:77-115) does all three, and the existing set_notifications action (topics_controller.rb:330-334) uses it. routes/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6:14 nulls details.notificationReasonText, which hides the stale reason on this one page only. Reasoned.
findings.reason: Appendix: two seats. Not fixed this loop. It will probably be resolved by the main-list nil-row fix if that fix switches to TopicUser.change.

findings.claim: The new render :show in perform_show_response runs before show sets canonical_url (line 87). Every server-rendered topic page, not just the new endpoint, therefore loses its <link rel=canonical> tag.
findings.evidence: show calls perform_show_response at line 85 and sets canonical_url at line 87. layouts/_head.html.erb:9 calls canonical_link_tag while @canonical_url is nil, and lib/canonical_url.rb:14 returns '' for nil. Proposed red test: a controller spec with render_views that expects response.body to include rel=canonical. Reasoned; not run.
findings.reason: Appendix: one seat. Not fixed under the merge rule. Flagged for attention because the claimed blast radius is every topics#show page, and no other seat assessed it.

findings.claim: An in-app Ember transition to topicUnsubscribe only loads topic JSON and never calls the server action, yet it still shows the 'You will stop receiving notifications' confirmation.
findings.evidence: Route lines 4-10 call only PostStream.loadTopicView (/t/:id.json). The state change exists only in the server-side HTML GET. Reasoned.
findings.reason: Appendix: two seats. ponytail listed it as out of lane and did not assess it, so it is not counted.

findings.claim: Hidden coupling. The shared unsubscribe_link string now needs %{unsubscribe_url}, so any MessageBuilder caller passing add_unsubscribe_link: true without unsubscribe_url: raises I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument (message_builder.rb:67, 90).
findings.evidence: The existing spec had to be patched (message_builder_spec.rb:172), showing the contract changed. In core only user_notifications.rb:294-295 sets the flag, and it passes the URL. open-code-review checked this and found core safe; superpowers agrees. The claim concerns plugins and future callers, and no seat disproves that.
findings.reason: Appendix: two seats. Core is not affected, according to all three seats that looked.

findings.claim: The 28 other server.*.yml locales keep the old unsubscribe_link string, so non-English users never see the per-topic link.
findings.evidence: superpowers finding 6. open-code-review noted the same gap but chose not to report it ('translation gap, not a crash'). mattpocock did not compare locales.
findings.reason: Appendix: one seat. A translation gap, normally handled by the translation workflow.

findings.claim: The List-Unsubscribe header still points to user preferences, not the per-topic URL.
findings.evidence: mattpocock finding 12 addendum. Reasoned.
findings.reason: Appendix: one seat, advisory.

findings.claim: status: 301 on a URL with side effects is a permanent, cacheable redirect. After a slug change, browsers follow the cached stale redirect and pay an extra hop through slugs_do_not_match; 302 is safer.
findings.evidence: superpowers finding 8. Reasoned.
findings.reason: Appendix: one seat.

findings.claim: Format-only and out-of-scope edits are mixed into a feature PR: about 100 of 225 changed lines. This breaches CONTRIBUTING.md §2 (one feature per branch) and the §4 note on style changes. Affected: topic_user.rb (all hunks), routes/topic-from-params.js.es6 (all hunks), views/email/notification.html.erb:1-29, lib/email/message_builder.rb:24-39,60,68, app/mailers/user_notifications.rb:310, the config/routes.rb:437-442 reorder, and the client.en.yml:1019 blank line.
findings.evidence: mattpocock findings 6 and 8 (the scope part), and ponytail finding 3 with line counts from git diff --stat. superpowers confirms topic_user.rb and notification.html.erb have no logic change.
findings.reason: Appendix: two seats, both advisory. Could be addressed later by moving these edits into a separate style commit.

findings.claim: A hidden behaviour change in the route reorder: the post_number: /\d+/ constraint was dropped from both summary routes.
findings.evidence: mattpocock finding 8 calls this an unrelated behaviour change. ponytail says neither summary path has a :post_number segment, so the constraint was inert. superpowers checked it and found the removal harmless because those routes have no such segment.
findings.reason: The behaviour-change claim is disproved by the ponytail and superpowers reports: the constraint applied to a segment the routes do not have, so dropping it changes nothing. The out-of-scope part of the same edit is kept in the reformatting appendix entry.

findings.claim: The rewritten tracking scope uses 3- and 5-space indents where the file uses 2-space nesting. This breaches CONTRIBUTING.md §3 (follow existing conventions).
findings.evidence: mattpocock finding 7.
findings.reason: Appendix: one seat, advisory.

findings.claim: constraints: {topic_id: /\d+/} has no spaces inside the braces, breaching CONTRIBUTING.md §4.
findings.evidence: mattpocock finding 9. The neighbouring lines share the same style, so this follows local precedent.
findings.reason: Appendix: one seat, advisory, and consistent with local precedent.

findings.claim: stopNotificiationsText is misspelled, and the typo appears in both the controller and templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs:3.
findings.evidence: mattpocock finding 10; ponytail finding 1 notes the misspelling.
findings.reason: Appendix: two seats. It would disappear if ponytail's controller deletion is ever taken.

findings.claim: The module ends with '})' and no semicolon, unlike every sibling .js.es6 controller.

findings.claim: The controller exists only to format one string. The i18n helper already accepts named params, so the template could use {{{i18n 'topic.unsubscribe.stop_notifications' title=model.fancyTitle}}} directly.
findings.evidence: helpers/i18n.js.es6 and register-unbound.js.es6:30 resolve hash params. templates/modal/change-owner.hbs:2 already uses the pattern. Whether this behaves the same after an in-place model change was not checked.

findings.claim: The view exists only to add classNames ['topic-unsubscribe']. The template's wrapper div (unsubscribe.hbs:1) could carry the class instead.
findings.evidence: The SCSS at common/base/topic.scss:67 only needs an ancestor with .topic-unsubscribe. The seat itself calls this a judgement call, since Discourse often pairs routes with views.
findings.reason: Appendix: one seat, advisory, and self-described as a judgement call.

coverage: Gate: not run (benchmark mode), so no finding is anchored by executed checks and the review is unanchored. No seat ran any test, so every failing test cited is a proposal, not a result. Spec: none was given; seats used the PR title 'FEATURE: per-topic unsubscribe option in emails' as the implicit spec. Standards: only CONTRIBUTING.md ('Code' and 'Coding Conventions'); there are no other standards docs. Files: every seat reports reading all 18 patch files, with these limits. mattpocock reviewed app/assets/stylesheets/common/base/topic.scss and views/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6 only lightly, did not render the Ember/Handlebars templates, and did not compare other-language locale files (outside the patch). open-code-review's tool excluded six .js.es6 files (unsupported_ext) and spec/components/email/message_builder_spec.rb (default_path); the seat reviewed them manually from the patch. superpowers checked app/models/topic_user.rb, app/views/email/notification.html.erb, topic.scss and views/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6 only for behaviour change. ponytail reviewed for over-engineering only. Axes and process: no reviewer from another model family took a correctness seat. ponytail's five 'outside my lane, not assessed' pointers were not counted as raising seats. No fresh verifier was dispatched (no agent access), but no correctness-seat Critical or Important finding was rejected, so none was needed. The only rejection is an advisory Minor claim disproved by two other seats' reports. Steps 5 and 6 (fix, re-review) were not run by instruction, so nothing has converged and all five main-list items remain open.
